title: tenant-residency-evidence-streamer-and-retention-controls-for-dedicated-nodes
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Customers using Dedicated capacity require verifiable proof that their tenant workloads and data remain within specified geographic/residency boundaries, that retention rules are applied, and that a reproducible, auditable artifact exists for compliance reviews. Current ad-hoc exports are manual and lack cryptographic binding to infrastructure topology and time.

Goal: Build an automated 'evidence streamer' and retention-control surface that continuously collects tenant-to-host mappings, configuration snapshots (retention settings, storage location, encryption state), signs evidence with a customer-scoped key (HSM/KMS), and exports tamper-evident artifacts to tenant-specific evidence stores or customer-provided S3 endpoints. Provide Console UI and APIs for on-demand attestations, scheduled reports, and retention policy enforcement logs.

Scope (MVP):
- Collector agent running on dedicated control-plane that samples active tenant allocations and node residency metadata (node IDs, region tag, AZ, instance id, image fingerprint, network CIDRs) every N minutes.
- Evidence signer service that creates a signed JSONL ledger of snapshots. Ledger entries include a Merkle root per batch and individual signed entries for machine verification. Support Redwood-managed KMS and optional customer-supplied signing key (KMS ExternalKey).
- Exporter that writes artifacts to: 1) Redwood evidence bucket (encrypted, lifecycle), 2) customer S3/GCS target (via secure cross-account role), 3) Console download for ad-hoc review.
- Retention enforcement controller: persistent config per-tenant (retention window, purge exceptions, legal-hold flag) with a background scrubber that enforces deletes and records purge actions as signed events.
- Audit API + Console pages: evidence history, coverage metrics, last-snapshot timestamp, on-demand attestation generation (PDF + verifiable JSON).

Technical approach and decisions:
- Chosen ledger model: append-only JSONL with per-batch Merkle root rather than a single global chain to balance proof compactness and storage operational cost. This lets us publish batch roots to an immutable store and verify individual entries without replaying entire chain.
- Signing and key management: integrate with Redwood KMS (AWS KMS/HSM) for hosted customers; expose an interface for customers to bring keys (via EKM or cross-account KMS). Signatures follow RFC7515 compact JWS for easy verification.
- Sampling cadence trade-off: default 10m cadence for active allocations; allow more frequent (1m) for high-security customers. This balances host churn noise and cost.
- Redaction: evidence contains node metadata but scrubs PII (user IDs, ephemeral container IDs) and stores only hashed identifiers when needed for cross-reference.
- Tamper-evidence: signed entries + published batch roots provide provable immutability. We will also store an audit manifest with the exporter operation and exporter nonce in a separate durable bucket with Object Lock enabled for customers requesting legal hold.

Testing & validation:
- Unit tests for collector mapping logic and signer.
- E2E in a dedicated staging cluster with synthetic tenant churn to validate coverage metrics and signature verification.
- Compliance runbook with simulated auditor requests (download artifacts, verify signatures, validate retention enforcement).

Rollout plan:
1) POC and security review (this ticket)
2) Internal alpha on Redwood-owned dedicated pool (1 week)
3) Closed beta with two customers (opt-in) and export-to-customer-S3 test (4 weeks)
4) Console surface and self-serve config (3 weeks)
5) GA for Dedicated tenants with opt-in policy and documentation

Risks & mitigations:
- Storage cost growth if cadence and retention windows are large. Mitigate with lifecycle policies (transition to Glacier-like tiers) and per-tenant quotas.
- Signing key compromise: provide key rotation docs and emergency re-signing procedures; store previous root indexes to allow proof continuity.
- Mis-attribution due to host reassignments: correlate allocation timestamps and use marker events (assignment-start/assignment-end) to establish residency windows.

Acceptance criteria:
- Evidence streamer produces signed snapshot artifacts at configurable cadence and stores them in tenant evidence buckets.
- Console shows evidence coverage >=99% for dedicated hosts within 10 minutes of assignment in alpha tests.
- Retention controller successfully enforces per-tenant retention rules and records purge events as signed audit entries.
- Security review completed and documentation published (Confluence), and a small customer closed beta completed with two enterprise customers.

2025-02-28 - Design sync with Console PM (Anya Rivera): Console should surface 'Evidence freshness' and allow admins to set retention windows and legal-hold via a guarded workflow. Need design spec for 1-click attestation download.
2025-03-02 - Engineering notes: Chose per-batch Merkle roots to keep verification cheap for auditors. Implemented signer shim and local verifier binary. Started integration tests with mocked KMS.

2025-03-04 - Liam O'Neill: Collated beta customer requirements: some want weekly signed snapshots only; others require daily snapshots plus immediate on-demand attestations. Added per-tenant cadence override to config API. Next: implement exporter retries and backpressure handling.
